strategies.name: Detecting Electron Application Abuse for Proxy Execution

analytics.name: Analytic 0071
analytics.guidance: Abuse of trusted Electron apps (Teams, Slack, Chrome) to spawn child processes or execute payloads via malicious command-line arguments (e.g., --gpu-launcher) and modified app resources (.asar). Behavior chain: suspicious parent process (Electron app) → unusual command-line args → child process creation → optional DLL/network artifacts.

tuning.description: Correlation window tying app launch, file tampering, child process, and network events (5–10 minutes typical).
Flag admin/service accounts versus standard users executing Electron apps.
Baseline of Electron-based executables expected in the enterprise.
Whitelist normal child processes (chrome.exe → crashpad_handler.exe) versus anomalies (powershell.exe).
Approved service domains for Teams, Slack, etc. to suppress benign traffic.
Expected hash/signature of app.asar resources to detect tampering.

analytics.name: Analytic 0072
analytics.guidance: Abuse of Linux Electron binaries by modifying app.asar or config JS files and spawning unexpected child processes (bash, curl, python).

tuning.description: Baseline of expected asar package signatures per app.
Flag shells/python spawned from Electron parent.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: Electron-based binary spawning shell or script interpreter

analytics.name: Analytic 0073
analytics.guidance: Abuse of macOS Electron apps by modifying app.asar bundles and spawning child processes (osascript, curl, sh) from Electron executables.

tuning.description: Baseline of legitimate Electron app paths under /Applications.
Alert when signed Electron parent spawns unsigned child.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Electron app spawning unexpected child process

log_sources.name: macos:osquery
log_sources.channel: CREATE/MODIFY: Modification of app.asar inside .app bundle
